title: Art Simms's band in Milwaukee, Bernie Young and commuting from school
summary: He plays Riverside Gardens in Milwaukee with Art Simms, with Preston Jackson, picked up at school; Bernie Young takes over after Simms dies.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Still going to school. And then that same band was taken over by Art Simms. He played violin and we got a job up in Milwaukee. Three nights a week.
Where in Milwaukee?
At Riverside Gardens.
Riverside Gardens?
Uh-huh.
Was that the same band, had a lot of Chicago men in it? Or it was a Chicago --

It was a Chicago band. See, because they used to come by Wendell Phillips and pick me up. See, we worked Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday. They'd come by Wendell Phillips High School and pick me up Wednesday afternoon. We'd go up there and play and come back Thursday morning and go to school Friday and Saturday, then they'd pick me up Saturday afternoon, then we'd go up and play Saturday and Sunday, and then bring me back Monday morning.
Do you remember who was in Art Simms' band?
One, I remember the trombone player, Preston Jackson.
Preston Jackson. Was Zilber Randolph in that band?
Later.
Later. That was after you --
After ART died, yeah. No, he was in the same time I was. See, Art Simms died, and Bernie Young took it over.
Right. Bernie Young's band.
Bernie Young's band.
That's a well-known band. They never recorded.
Never -- no, I don't think so.
But I've read about it. And I interviewed Zilmer Randolph on the same project that I'm doing you. And he was telling me about that band, said it was really a good band.
It was. Yes, it was.
Well, how long were you with that band?

I stayed with that band about six months. Then I left and gigged around Chicago for a little while, and then I went back with Art Simms. When I went back with Art Simms is when he died. And I stayed with Bernie Young, oh, I guess for about -- almost a year.
